note: Horizontal chrome in DIPs: how much width a control consumes around its content (padding + border + glyph + dropdown). Measured with WPF, not hand-copied: prototype/ChromeGen places content of known width in each control; prototype/LayoutOracle shows real off-screen windows and compares them with the resolver. Describes the default templates of built-in WPF controls only.
fieldsNote: chromeWidth already INCLUDES the default Padding and BorderThickness. 'padding' and 'border' are the values in effect with the default template (left + right). 'paddingMode' / 'borderMode' say what an explicit value does, as confirmed case by case with LayoutOracle: 'replace' = it replaces the default one-for-one; 'ignore' = the default template does not use the property at all; absent = not confirmed, so the explicit value is added on top (over-deducts, the safe direction). 'stylePadding' is what {TemplateBinding Padding} yields in a custom template when it differs from 'padding'.
scrollBarWidthNote: SystemParameters.VerticalScrollBarWidth in DIPs varies with display scaling. prototype/DpiProbe (GetSystemMetricsForDpi): 17.00 at 100%, 16.80 at 125%, 17.33 at 150%, 17.14 at 175%, 17.00 at 200%. 17.5 is a ceiling over all of them: under-deducting would over-estimate the available width.
windowFrameNote: Window.Width is the OUTER width. Measured at 125% scaling: standard frame 14.4 DIP (18 px), ThreeDBorderWindow 17.6 DIP (22 px), WindowStyle=None with a resizable frame 12.8 DIP; no frame for WindowStyle=None with NoResize/CanMinimize, AllowsTransparency, or WindowChrome. The values here are the 100%-scaling figures (16 px / 20 px), which are the largest in DIPs: prototype/DpiProbe (AdjustWindowRectExForDpi) gives the standard frame as 16 / 14.4 / 14.67 / 13 DIP at 100 / 125 / 150 / 200%, ThreeDBorderWindow 20 at 100%, WindowStyle=None resizable 14 at 100%.

CheckBox.note: the default template adds Padding 4,-1,0,0 through a HasContent trigger; chromeWidth includes it

Window.note: the frame is separate, see windowFrame

ComboBox.note: measured via the templated content host (content width does not propagate)

TabControl.note: LayoutOracle: content of a 400-wide TabControl is 394; the TabItem's own Padding/Margin style the header, not the content

TextBox.note: measured via the templated content host (content width does not propagate)

PasswordBox.note: measured via the templated content host (content width does not propagate)

StatusBar.note: LayoutOracle: 300-wide StatusBar leaves 294 inside a StatusBarItem (item chrome 6)

ScrollViewer.note: the vertical scroll bar; see scrollBarWidth

ListBox.note: measured via the templated content host (content width does not propagate)

ListView.note: measured via the templated content host (content width does not propagate)

ItemsControl.note: measured via the templated content host (content width does not propagate)

headersNote: Chrome around the HEADER of a control, which differs from the chrome around its content. LayoutOracle: a long header in a 300-wide GroupBox shows 291, in a 300-wide Expander 273; a 150-wide DataGrid column shows 140 of its header, a 150-wide GridViewColumn 146.
